name: Viz.ai
short_description: Detects suspected stroke from CT scans, notifying specialists in seconds.
why_relevant: Proof that AI triage changes a 30-minute clot call into an instant one.
history: Founded in 2016 by a neurosurgeon, a venture investor and data scientists, Viz.ai set out to shave minutes off stroke care. Its AI analyzes CT angiograms and automatically pages the right specialist, and in 2018 the company earned the first FDA clearance for an AI triage algorithm. Viz.ai broadened into pulmonary embolism, aortic and cervical spine screening, and went public through a SPAC merger in 2021. Its platform now serves more than 1,800 hospitals, and the company has expanded from detection into AI-powered care coordination.

name: Qure.ai
short_description: Tuberculosis and chest X-ray AI accurate enough for WHO-grade programs.
why_relevant: AI that screens TB at scale in low-resource clinics.
history: Qure.ai spun out of the analytics firm Fractal in 2016 with a mission to make expert-level medical imaging accessible in clinics that lack radiologists. Its qXR chest X-ray algorithm became a foundation of WHO-backed tuberculosis screening programs, and FDA clearances for head trauma analysis and chest radiographs extended its reach. With deployments in more than 100 countries and tens of millions of scans read, Qure.ai has grown from imaging tools into end-to-end digital care, connecting sicker patients identified by AI with clinicians and treatment pathways.

name: Niramai
short_description: Non-contact thermal imaging plus AI for early breast lesion detection.
why_relevant: Radiation-free, privacy-friendly screening suited to community clinics.
history: Niramai was founded in 2016 by researchers from the Indian Institute of Science to bring breast screening to clinics with no imaging equipment. Its Thermalytix system uses a high-resolution thermal sensor and machine learning to detect early breast lesions without radiation or physical contact. Having screened more than 100,000 women in hospitals and mobile clinics across India, Niramai has won awards from international health bodies and backing from investors including pi Ventures, positioning it as a scalable, privacy-safe answer to breast cancer screening in underserved regions.

name: Ezra
short_description: Scans 13 organs for cancer in an hour with AI-guided MRI.
why_relevant: Turns the oncologist's once-per-life scan into an annual subscription.
history: Ezra was founded in 2018 by entrepreneur Emi Gal to turn whole-body cancer screening into a fast, repeatable checkup. Its MRI scans read up to 13 organs in roughly an hour, guided by AI that shortens scan times and highlights suspicious tissues. The company opened screening centers in New York, Palo Alto, and beyond, and raised a $61 million Series B to fund larger scanners able to cover more organs. Ezra now markets a subscription model that recasts the once-per-lifetime cancer scan as an annual health habit.

name: Omada Health
short_description: Digital programs for diabetes, weight and cardiovascular care.
why_relevant: Outcomes-based digital health at employer scale with peer-reviewed results.
history: Omada Health was founded in San Francisco in 2011 by Sean Duffy and Adrian James after a family encounter with prediabetes. Its digital diabetes prevention program pairs connected scales and glucose readings with human coaches, and it was one of the first digital programs of its scale to publish peer-reviewed clinical results. Backed by more than half a billion dollars from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Omada expanded into hypertension and cardiovascular care, and its programs are now contracted by employers and health plans across the United States.

name: Hinge Health
short_description: Musculoskeletal digital therapy with sensors and coaching, now public.
why_relevant: Displaces opioid-centered back pain with app-delivered physical therapy.
history: Hinge Health was founded in 2015 by Daniel Perez, an exercise scientist, and Gabriel Mecklenburg, a physician, to treat musculoskeletal pain without opioids. Its app connects wearable sensors, guided exercise, and health coaching, and publishes trials showing results comparable to in-person physical therapy. The company scaled through employers and health plans, built its own Enso wearable, and completed an initial public offering in 2025, becoming one of the first digital musculoskeletal specialists to reach the public market.

name: Oura
short_description: Smart ring measuring sleep, recovery and readiness trends.
why_relevant: Turned the ring into the standard consumer health companion.
history: Oura began in 2013 in Oulu, Finland, where a team of engineers set out to track sleep in a ring. The device measures sleep stages, body temperature, and readiness, and won early fame through partnerships with the NBA and Formula 1, plus research with hospitals on fever and night-shift monitoring. Millions of rings have been sold on a hardware-plus-subscription model, and Oura has expanded into medical studies, corporate wellness, and new sensing hardware, cementing the smart ring as a mainstream health companion.

name: Whoop
short_description: Recovery and strain wearable used by professional athletes.
why_relevant: Defines the training-load metric now standard in elite sport.
history: Whoop was founded in 2012 by Will Ahmed in his Harvard dorm room to quantify the balance between training strain and recovery. The company made a breakthrough with a subscription-only wrist strap that measures recovery, strain, and sleep around the clock, and its metrics were adopted across the NFL, NBA, and MLB. Millions of dollars flowed from investors and athlete backers like Michael Phelps and Patrick Mahomes, and Whoop reached a valuation of $3.6 billion while expanding into stress, heart-rate, and female health monitoring.

name: Cala Health
short_description: Wearable neurostimulation that suppresses essential tremor.
why_relevant: Addressed a tremor without drugs or brain surgery.
history: Cala Health was founded in 2014 by neurologist Kate Rosenbluth to treat movement disorders without invasive surgery. Its Cala Trio device delivers targeted peripheral stimulation to the wrist during tremor episodes, and in 2018 it became the first FDA-cleared wearable therapy for essential tremor. Backed by more than $100 million in funding from investors including GV and Johnson & Johnson, Cala is now exploring applications for balance, Parkinson's disease, and depression, broadening peripheral neuromodulation into a treatment category of its own.

name: NeuroPace
short_description: RNS system senses and stops seizures in drug-resistant epilepsy.
why_relevant: The only responsive neurostimulator approved for seizure prevention.
history: NeuroPace was founded in 1997 to build an implant that could respond to seizures as they begin. Its Responsive Neurostimulation (RNS) System reads brain signals through electrodes and delivers brief stimulation when abnormal activity appears, earning FDA approval in 2013 for adults with drug-resistant epilepsy. The company went public on Nasdaq in 2021 under the ticker NPCE and has built a large implanted-user base, with long-term registry data supporting outcomes such as reduced seizure frequency and improved quality of life.

name: Nalu Medical
short_description: Percutaneous electrical stimulation for chronic back pain.
why_relevant: Smaller implant than incumbents opens neuromodulation to more patients.
history: Nalu Medical was founded in 2014 to shrink neurostimulation implants that treat chronic back and leg pain. Its micro-sized implantable pulse generator, cleared by the FDA for peripheral and spinal cord stimulation, is placed through a needle in an outpatient procedure, far smaller than conventional devices. Backed by more than $300 million across rounds led by investors such as MVM Partners and Pura Vida, Nalu has built a commercial footprint spanning pain clinics in the United States and Europe and continues to expand its indications.

name: Bigfoot Biomedical
short_description: Smart insulin delivery system using calibrated insulin data.
why_relevant: Simplifies insulin decisions for people with diabetes.
history: Bigfoot Biomedical was founded in 2014 by veterans of diabetes device companies to simplify insulin management. Its Unity system pairs smart pen caps with Abbott's glucose data to recommend insulin doses, and the FDA cleared the system for daily insulin therapy in 2021. After a financing round led by Abbott, the company was acquired by Abbott in 2023. The technology now sits inside Abbott's connected care portfolio, applying automated dose advice to millions of people on insulin therapy.

name: DarioHealth
short_description: Smart glucose monitors combined with coaching programs.
why_relevant: Consumer-priced connected glucose management sold at scale.
history: DarioHealth began in Israel in 2011 with a pocket-sized glucose monitor that plugged into a smartphone, pairing readings with automated coaching. The company, dual-headquartered with New York, went public on Nasdaq in 2019 and expanded from diabetes into hypertension, metabolic health, and behavioral health. Through acquisitions such as Upright and Way to Well, and partnerships with insurers and employers, Dario now sells integrated multi-condition care programs that combine medical devices, data, and coaching across the United States and Europe.

name: Vida Health
short_description: Digital health marketplace pairing patients with coaches and clinicians.
why_relevant: Bundled chronic-condition programs delivered through one app.
history: Vida Health was founded in 2014 by Stephanie Tilenius to create one connected home for chronic-care coaching. Its network matches patients with health coaches, dietitians, and therapists through a single app, and its programs address diabetes, heart health, and mental health. Vida raised more than $200 million and became a valued partner to employers and health plans, expanding through acquisitions in behavioral health. The company's model bundled fragmented point solutions into one reimbursable platform backed by published outcomes.

name: Akili Interactive
short_description: FDA-cleared video game therapy for ADHD in children.
why_relevant: First prescription digital therapeutic cleared as a real medicine.
history: Akili Interactive was founded in 2011 by neuroscientists and game developers to turn attention training into therapy. Its ADHD treatment EndeavorRx became the first prescription digital therapeutic to receive FDA clearance in 2020 after randomized trials in children. Akili went public through a merger with Social Capital Suvretta in 2022, and in 2024 agreed to be acquired by Virtual Therapeutics. The company's journey helped establish a regulatory and commercial path for software prescribed as medicine.

name: Wysa
short_description: Rapidly deployable AI chatbot delivering mental-health support.
why_relevant: A six-week care-for-everyone AI therapist adopted by NHS mental health.
history: Wysa was founded in 2014 by Jo Aggarwal, a former business consultant, and Ramakant Vempati, an AI engineer, to offer mental-health support that anyone can access with a smartphone. Its AI companion, built on cognitive-behavioral techniques, was adopted by NHS mental health services and won a U.S. FDA Breakthrough Device designation in 2021. Wysa has raised tens of millions of dollars and now works with health systems in the UK, India, Australia, and the United States, deploying its assistant for everything from waiting-list triage to daily self-care.

name: Woebot Health
short_description: Automated 24/7 cognitive-behavioral support from clinical trials.
why_relevant: Proved chatbot-delivered CBT matches clinician effectiveness in trials.
history: Woebot Health was founded in 2017 by clinical psychologist Alison Darcy out of Stanford University to deliver cognitive-behavioral therapy through conversation. Its chatbot connects with users in brief daily dialogues, and randomized trials have shown effects comparable to clinician-delivered CBT for both depression and substance-use challenges. The company raised a $90 million Series B led by Jazz Venture Partners and refocused its product roadmap on prescription-grade mental health treatments, reinforcing chatbots as a credible, scalable clinical channel.

name: K Health
short_description: AI intake that triages symptoms before a physician visit.
why_relevant: Machine-first triage that keeps primary care affordable.
history: K Health was founded in 2016 by Allon Bloch, Ran Shaul, and Jesse Rabinowitz to apply anonymized data from millions of medical records to everyday symptom triage. Its app helps people understand symptoms, connects them to 24/7 doctors, and tracks chronic conditions, reaching millions of users worldwide through direct consumer access and insurer partnerships. The New York-based company's 2024 Series E valuation placed it above $1 billion, and it has expanded from chat into primary care, specialty referrals, and insurer-backed clinic access.

name: Forward
short_description: AI-bodied clinics with continuous monitoring and precision medicine.
why_relevant: Rebuilt the clinic touchpoints around algorithms and sensors.
history: Forward was founded in 2016 by Adrian Aoun, a former Google executive, plus Ilya Abyzov, to rebuild primary care around continuous sensing and algorithms. Its membership clinics feature AI-driven intake, body-scan booths, and 24/7 remote care, opening its first location in San Francisco in 2017. After raising more than $200 million from investors such as Founders Fund, Forward expanded into multiple cities and employer partnerships, trying to prove that machine-first preventive medicine can be delivered at consumer scale.

name: Carbon Health
short_description: Fast hybrid urgent-care model with an integrated EHR.
why_relevant: Same-day accessible primary care whose software is the moat.
history: Carbon Health was founded in 2015 by Eren Bali and Emin Yilmaz, creators of Udemy, to build the care model they believed chain clinics deserved: fast visits backed by real software. Its hybrid urgent-care clinics and proprietary EHR grew quickly, and the company became a key COVID-19 testing and vaccination provider during the pandemic. With more than $500 million raised, Carbon opened dozens of clinics and later pivoted toward insurer and employer partnerships, pairing the EHR with enterprise telehealth offerings.

name: Teladoc Health
short_description: Global virtual care company for millions of members.
why_relevant: Scaled the enterprise telehealth category from startups to insurers.
history: Teladoc traces its roots to 2002, when Michael Gorton launched a telephone-based medical consultation service in Texas. The company became the defining enterprise telehealth platform, went public in 2015, and in 2020 completed the $18.5 billion merger with Livongo that paired virtual visits with chronic-condition data. Teladoc Health now serves tens of millions of members globally across urgent care, mental health, and chronic-care programs, and has expanded into AI-enabled documentation and international markets.

name: Osso VR
short_description: VR surgical training checked for skills transfer by clinical trials.
why_relevant: VR sim proved to double technique scores versus textbook training.
history: Osso VR was founded in 2016 by orthopedic surgeon Justin Barad to make surgical training safer and more repeatable inside virtual reality. Its immersive simulations let surgeons rehearse procedures, and peer-reviewed trials found that Osso-trained surgeons scored roughly twice as high as controls on technique. With more than $90 million raised from investors such as Accel and Jazz, Osso has built curricula with device makers including Zimmer Biomet and Johnson & Johnson, and its platform now spans multiple specialties and global training partnerships.

name: Vicarious Surgical
short_description: Single-port surgical robot with human-like wrist camera control.
why_relevant: Publicly traded bet that one small port can perform whole operations.
history: Vicarious Surgical was founded in 2015 by two MIT engineering alumni who set out to shrink surgical robotics down to a single incision. Its humanoid-arms system is inserted through one small port and guided by a camera controlled like a human wrist. A 2021 SPAC merger brought the company to the New York Stock Exchange at a valuation near $1 billion, and the firm has since focused on design refinements and FDA clearance to bring single-port robotics into mainstream operating rooms.

name: Limbic
short_description: AI triage and therapist-assist that won UK clinical-grade recognition.
why_relevant: First AI approved as a Class IIa medical device for therapy in the NHS.
history: Limbic was founded in London in 2017 by computational neuroscientists Ross Harper and Mario Ragucci, alongside professor Anil Seth, to apply neural networks to mental health referral. Its AI handles self-referral, assessment, and therapist support within UK talking-therapy services, and Limbic Care became the first AI assistant certified as a Class IIa medical device for therapy in the NHS, in 2022. The platform has processed millions of patient interactions, and Limbic now sells AI triage and analytics to health systems internationally.

name: Alto Pharmacy
short_description: Same-day pharmacy delivery with insurance-friendly savings.
why_relevant: Operationally deep patient-first pharmacy expressed in software.
history: Alto Pharmacy was founded in 2015 in San Francisco by Jamie Karraker and co-founders to rebuild the pharmacy around the patient. Its same-day delivery, insurance automation, and in-app consultation turned a sprawling prescription process into a convenient digital loop, and the company reached a valuation above $1 billion. Alto expanded from urban on-demand delivery into specialty and chronic medication management, and while digital-pharmacy valuations cooled in the mid-2020s, the company remains one of the most operationally innovative software-native pharmacies in the United States.

name: Notable
short_description: Automates prior authorization and care intake with voice AI.
why_relevant: Removes the paper-shuffling that kills hours of clinical time.
history: Notable was founded in 2017 by Pranay Kapadia to apply intelligent agents to healthcare administration. Its voice and document automation handles prior authorization, referral management, and intake across large health systems, claiming to save provider organizations millions of administrative hours. The company raised more than $100 million, including a Series B led by ICONIQ Growth in 2024, and evolved from single-task tools into end-to-end autonomous workflows that sit between clinicians, payers, and patients.

name: Ada Health
short_description: AI health guide that assesses symptoms across forty-plus languages.
why_relevant: Clinically validated symptom engine deployed by health systems globally.
history: Ada Health was founded in Berlin in 2016 by mathematician Daniel Nathrath, physician-scientist Martin Hirsch, and doctor Claire Novorol to give everyone a clinically grounded way to understand symptoms. Its award-winning app assesses symptoms in more than forty languages, and partnerships with Bayer, Samsung, and health systems in Africa and Asia have widened its reach. With tens of millions of users and regulatory clearances in several markets, Ada now licenses its clinical reasoning engine to hospitals, insurers, and wearable makers.

name: Maven Clinic
short_description: Virtual clinic for reproduction and newborn-family care.
why_relevant: Highest-value unicorn in the women's and family health category.
history: Maven Clinic was founded in 2014 by Katherine Ryder to bring specialized care to women and families through a single digital clinic. Its network covers fertility, pregnancy, parenting, and pediatrics, served through employers and health plans, and the company became a unicorn with a $90 million round in 2022. Maven has supported more than 20 million members, expanded into benefits like surrogacy and doula support, and built clinical programs with published outcomes for conditions where women's health has long been underserved.

name: Carrot Fertility
short_description: Global fertility care-from-benefits platform for employers.
why_relevant: Makes IVF and surrogacy affordable through employer partnership.
history: Carrot Fertility was founded in 2016 by physician Asima Ahmad and entrepreneur Tammy Sun to make fertility care a mainstream employee benefit. Its global platform helps employers offer IVF, egg freezing, surrogacy, and menstrual health support across more than 100 countries, pairing localized care networks with clinical guidance. Carrot reached a valuation above $1 billion in a 2021 funding round, and has since deepened its family-building and fertility-preservation programs for corporate clients worldwide.

name: Cedar
short_description: Patient payment platform that improves billing experience for hospitals.
why_relevant: Turns hospital bills into a clear conversational payment flow.
history: Cedar was founded in 2016 by Florian Otto and Arel Lidow to transform the hospital bill into a clear, personalized conversation. Its payment and financial-engagement platform guides patients through explanations, payment plans, and support across hundreds of health systems. The company raised roughly $200 million, including a Series C led by Andreessen Horowitz and Franklin Templeton, and later added AI-driven tools for claim discovery and revenue integrity, now steering millions of patient payment interactions each year.
